# Security Checklist: Feedback Sweep, slice 1 of 2 — the checkpoint

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality gate on the trust boundary. This feature carries
public pull-request text into agents that edit the planning artifacts, so the
requirements governing that path must be complete, unambiguous, and mechanically
enforceable rather than stated as prose intent.
**Created**: 2026-08-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**Focus areas**: the author-association allowlist and where it is enforced;
untrusted-comment disposition and re-run safety; the shell-argument boundary in
both directions; the two named edge cases — a trusted author quoting untrusted
text, and a trusted comment naming an edit target outside the three artifacts.
**Depth**: release gate. **Audience**: reviewer (PR).

## Trust Boundary — Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is the author-association allowlist stated as a closed, enumerated set rather than as a description of who is trusted? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK002 Are all eight source-vocabulary values enumerated so that a ninth value is distinguishable from an untrusted one? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Is a ninth or unknown association value specified as a malformed observation rather than silently treated as untrusted? [Edge Case, Contract §Preconditions]
- [ ] CHK004 Do the requirements state which component enforces the allowlist, rather than leaving enforcement to orchestrator judgment? [Clarity, Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the allowlist's status as a proxy for write access — rather than a permissions check — recorded so no later reader mistakes it for one? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK006 Is a fixture required for each of the five excluded association values, named individually rather than as a group? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008a]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the required disposition wording for an untrusted comment fixed as a specific string rather than left to the implementation? [Measurability, Spec §FR-005]
- [x] CHK008 Do the requirements state that classification consumes only the helper's candidate list, so an untrusted body the orchestrator still holds in its own observation cannot reach an analyst by a second path? [Resolved, Plan §Trust Boundary Enforcement 2]
- [x] CHK009 Is the trust unit stated explicitly — the comment's author association, not the provenance of the text the comment contains — so that a trusted account quoting untrusted text is a recorded, accepted position rather than an unexamined one? [Resolved, Spec §Assumptions]

## Untrusted-Comment Disposition — Re-run Safety

- [ ] CHK010 Are the requirements explicit that an excluded comment produces no Feedback Sweep Log row, so a later run cannot read it as already handled? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK011 Is every exclusion required to be reported, so a dropped candidate is visible rather than silent? [Completeness, Contract §Output rules]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the exclusion-reason vocabulary closed, with exactly one reason per excluded comment? [Clarity, Data-model §3]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the invariant that observed equals candidates plus excluded stated as a requirement, so nothing is dropped without a disposition? [Measurability, Contract §Output rules]
- [ ] CHK014 Do the requirements prohibit posting a reply to an untrusted comment, rather than leaving reply scope to be inferred from the handled-comment definition? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK015 Is a run report defined on the proceed path, where no amendment occurred, so FR-005's requirement that every untrusted comment appear in the run report has a surface to appear on? [Resolved, Spec §FR-018a]

## Shell-Argument Boundary

- [ ] CHK016 Is the no-comment-text-in-a-shell-argument constraint stated for both directions, read and write, rather than for replies alone? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004b]
- [ ] CHK017 Are the write-side mechanics specified concretely — body passed by file path — rather than as an intent to avoid inlining? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004b]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the read-side mechanics specified concretely — query passed by file or by structured argument? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004b]
- [x] CHK019 Is the verification method for the shell boundary named, and does it cover the read direction as well as the reply direction that Scenario 4 pins? [Resolved, Plan §Trust Boundary Enforcement 6]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the constraint stated as a correction to the shipped precedent it contradicts, so it cannot be read as inherited and left unproven? [Traceability, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK021 Are the runner-side guarantees — `shell=False`, argument arrays, structured JSON on stdin — stated as requirements rather than as implementation preference? [Measurability, Plan §Constraints]

## Prompt-Kind Recognition — the Injection-Adjacent Path

- [ ] CHK022 Is the safety rationale for registering the `prompt` kind stated, rather than the registry being justified on completeness alone? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007c]
- [x] CHK023 Do the requirements specify what a recognized lead is replaced by in the payload handed to a consensus analyst, rather than only that it is "carried as metadata"? [Resolved, Spec §FR-007e]
- [ ] CHK024 Is it stated that recognition alone does not distrust a comment, so a recognized export still passes the allowlist and is still classified normally? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007c]
- [ ] CHK025 Is recognition prevented from forcing a class, with the single empty-export exception named? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007d]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the registry required to be derived from the shipped manifest and templates by a test, so a reworded lead fails loudly rather than silently disabling recognition? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008a]
- [ ] CHK027 Is the ambiguous-template case specified, given that several shipped templates declare an identical empty-export sentence? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007a]

## Self-Reply Exclusion — Spoof Resistance

- [ ] CHK028 Are both halves of the self-reply test stated as jointly required, with the failure mode of each half alone named? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the marker match specified as anchored at the start of the body rather than as a substring search anywhere in it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the reason anchoring defeats the quoting case stated, rather than left as an unexplained implementation detail? [Clarity, Data-model §3]
- [ ] CHK031 Is a marker collision required to be reported as a named exclusion rather than dropped silently? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK032 Is the marker specified as an HTML comment that renders as nothing, with the reason a visible sentence was rejected recorded? [Traceability, Spec §FR-015]
- [x] CHK033 Are validation rules defined for the authenticated-account input that supplies the author half of the test, given that an absent or wrong value silently disables that half and reopens the non-convergence FR-006a describes? [Resolved, Plan §Trust Boundary Enforcement 5]
- [ ] CHK034 Is the convergence consequence of a failed self-reply exclusion stated, so the requirement reads as load-bearing rather than as hygiene? [Traceability, Spec §FR-006a]

## Amendment Scope — What an Edit May Touch

- [x] CHK035 Do the requirements constrain the amendment edit surface as an enforced rule, rather than naming the three artifacts only as the expected destinations of a well-behaved edit? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012b]
- [x] CHK036 Is behavior specified for a trusted comment whose requested edit names a path outside the three artifacts — which class it takes, what the reviewer is told, and whether the run stops? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012b rule 1]
- [x] CHK037 Is the amendment commit's staged path set specified, so one amendment cannot carry an unrelated file along with it? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012b]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the one-commit-per-amendment rule stated with its forcing reasons, so it cannot be collapsed into a single run-wide commit? [Traceability, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the bookkeeping commit required to stage the workflow file path alone rather than the containing directory? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012a]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK040 Can the zero-untrusted-edits criterion be objectively verified against the fixture corpus? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK041 Does the determinism criterion enumerate the specific fixture shapes it is proved by, rather than asserting determinism generally? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the shell-boundary criterion stated with an inspection method rather than as an absolute claim with no evidence path? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK043 Does the log-integrity criterion cover both reviewer-derived prose hazards — an embedded pipe and an embedded newline — and the unresolvable-author case? [Coverage, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK044 Are the escaping rules tied to the specific downstream reader they protect, so the requirement is verifiable against a real parser rather than a general nicety? [Traceability, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK045 Is the assumption that registered sentences are stable strings on shipped pages recorded, together with what makes a drift loud? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK046 Is the absence of an operator override on this fail-closed gate recorded as a named, owner-less gap rather than omitted? [Assumption, Spec §Non-Goals]
- [ ] CHK047 Is the reliance on the existing consensus machinery stated as reuse without modification, so this slice adds a caller and not a new protocol? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK048 Is the per-comment byte budget justified by the runner limit it protects against, including why one oversized body would otherwise fail an entire sweep? [Traceability, Spec §FR-008]

## Second-Pass Items — Assessing the Remediation Itself

Added on the verification pass, which re-assessed the amended requirements
rather than only confirming the first-pass gaps had closed. Both items are
about text this remediation introduced.

- [x] CHK049 Does FR-007e's "every registered line the helper matched" agree with the helper envelope, which reports a singular `matched_line`? If a body carries two registered leads, the requirement removes both while the envelope names one, and the second survives into the analyst payload. [Resolved, Contract §Recognition — the envelope now reports `matched_lines`]
- [x] CHK050 Does the FR-012b rule 2 write-time stop specify a report shape, given that FR-017 and FR-019 both fix one for their stops? [Resolved, Plan §Trust Boundary Enforcement 4]

CHK049 was **not** closed here, because its resolution changes either a
requirement or the helper contract, and the contract sat outside this
remediation's edit surface. It closed later, at implementation task T001, which
owns the contract: the envelope's singular `matched_line` became
`matched_lines`, an ascending list of every matched registered line, so the
requirement and the envelope now agree and no second lead survives into the
analyst payload.
